title: Aankh ka Raaz: BHAGWAN ne Banayi ya EVOLUTION ne? | Hindi Auto-Dubbed
description:
The eye didn’t appear fully formed. It evolved. In this video, we trace the evolution of the eye from light-sensing eyespot cells in microbes to ocelli in planarians, to compound eyes in insects, and the camera-type eyes of vertebrates. We unpack Darwin’s often-misquoted passage and show how step-by-step natural selection and intermediate forms make complex vision inevitable. 

Meet pax-6, the master control gene behind eye formation across species, and see why convergent evolution gave cephalopods a sharper wiring while our own retina runs “backwards,” creating a blind spot that no intelligent designer would brag about. 

Along the way we visit the Cambrian and Burgess Shale, learn from blind cavefish (Mexican tetra) and the blind mole rat how evolution also removes organs, and explore pseudogenes and olfactory-receptor losses in primates that traded smell for trichromatic vision. Then we compare our eyesight with champions: the mantis shrimp with 12–16 receptors and polarization vision, tarsiers with night-adapted saucer eyes, scallops that focus images with mirror cups, dragonflies with near-360° motion vision, and bees reading UV nectar guides. 

If you’ve searched for Darwin eye quote explained, pax-6 gene, camera vs compound eye, blind spot design flaw, or why cephalopod eyes lack a blind spot, this is your clear, evidence-based walkthrough of how vision really evolved.
